newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan govt imposes sanctions on Nomura, DKB.
newsitem.headline: Japan govt imposes sanctions on Nomura, DKB.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) said on Wednesday it had imposed sanctions on Nomura Securities Co Ltd and Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank(DKB) in connection with scandals involving Japanese racketeers.
Nomura was ordered to halt its own-account stock-related dealing, including options and index trading, from August 6 to December 31.

MOF said in a statement it will also suspend Nomura's stock-related business at all branches from August 6 to August 12, while securities trading and securities futures broking at the first corporate division at Nomura headquarters will be suspended from August 6 to December 5.

Meanwhile, the MOF ordered DKB not to give new corporate clients credits from August 6 until year end, underwrite public bond issues for the same period, or undertake new business in Japan or abroad from August 6 until August 5, 1998.
The first corporate division is one of two such divisions at Nomura, and is the department that managed an account linked to a "sokaiya" racketeer.
The head office as a whole, excluding the first corporate division, will be suspended from securities trading and securities futures broking from August 6 to September 5.

Nomura will also be barred from participating in the auction and underwriting of public bonds, including Japanese government bonds (JGBs), municipal bonds and government-guaranteed bonds, from August 6 to December 31.
Both Nomura and DKB have admitted to giving loans to Japanese racketeers in violation of Japan's Commercial Code.
Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita said on Wednesday the central bank did not see the scandal undermining the bank's financial soundness.
Matsushita said in a statement: The Bank of Japan does not see the scandal over Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank and Nomura Securities greatly undermining their financial soundness."
